method: Re-extracted the adopted curriculum and entry requirements from a separately retrieved PDF, checked the dated course periods and underlying descriptions, then read the finished schedules and reconsidered the content and placements against the current workbook.
findings: The standard English variant has 60 EC per year. The 42 EC threshold and named year-one courses are satisfied before year two. Both block 4 Exploration courses are possible once both first-year courses have been completed and there is no concurrent registration. One example has the regional course in block 1 and the elective in semester 2. Second-year fieldwork is followed by one theme and matching presentation each semester in year three.

The required year-two project is the anchor for optional independent research. It includes group fieldwork and individual writing. The degree has no separately credited final-year thesis. The elective spaces and linked presentations remain distinct from UCR course matches.

The closest plan uses social theory, ethnographic methods and historical and political inquiry. Ecology and environmental justice shape the second plan, while documentary, museum and media studies shape the third. The approaches are distinct and the proposed alignments describe bounded overlap. Course descriptions and the audience notes agree with the reviewed source material.
